label: Card Feedback
title: Card Feedback
summary: Use a Card Feedback to show the result of an action in the page, such as a payment that went through or failed, with one next step.
corePrinciple: Say what happened, then what to do next.

anatomy.title: An icon, the outcome, and a next step
anatomy.description: A tinted panel stacks a status icon, a title, one line of detail, and an optional row of buttons. You build it from the card’s parts: Icon, Content, Title, Body, and Action.
blocks: CardFeedback.Icon: a 20 px registry icon in the status colour.
CardFeedback.Title: the outcome in a few words, 14 px.
CardFeedback.Body: one sentence of detail, 12 px; it wraps.
CardFeedback.Action: a row of small buttons in the status colour.

configuration.title: Three statuses
configuration.description: AppearanceSystem sets the status: positive, the default, is green; warning is orange; negative is red. It colours the panel, the icon, and the buttons in Action. Pick an icon that matches: the card colours it but doesn’t choose it. AppearanceBrand only shifts the title and body colour slightly.

states.title: With or without actions
states.description: The card itself is static: only the buttons you put in Action respond. onPress makes the whole card one button instead; use it only when the card has no buttons inside, and name it with accessibilityLabel. A pressable card fades slightly on hover and more while pressed, and shows a ring on keyboard focus. disabled fades it to half and ignores presses.

sizing.title: Your screen sets the width
sizing.description: The card fills its host’s width; Figma draws it at 328 px. It’s as tall as its content and at least 59 px, with 12 px padding and 8 px between the icon, the text, and the actions. Title and body wrap, and buttons wrap onto a new row when they run out of room.

content.title: The outcome, then the next step
content.description: Make the title the outcome, such as “Payment failed”, and the body one sentence on what it means for the person. Label each button with a verb, and keep to one or two. The colour alone doesn’t carry the status for everyone, so the title has to say it.
blocks: “Payment failed”, what happened to the money, and “Try again”.
specimen: Your bank declined the payment. No money was taken.

inContext.title: A failed payment on the Pay screen
inContext.description: Try again runs the screen’s own retry through the button’s onPress. When the retry goes through, the screen swaps the card for a positive one; the card doesn’t change itself or time out.

sources.title: Use the public Card Feedback contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at c7d3348 (19 October) and taken from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card/Feedback is one 328 × 123 component with no properties; its status comes from modes, and its icon is a solid circle, while the package draws whichever registry icon you pass. The card doesn’t read the app’s theme, so Color Mode has to come through its modes. Inside a VStack or another Coin container that passes modes down, its parts keep the card’s status colours. Emphasis alone doesn’t quieten a button in the status colour, so the quieter action here switches to Brand Neutral at Emphasis Low. The published Storybook hasn’t been rebuilt: it still renders every story as a pressable card with buttons inside it, and shows the older generated page.
